title: xcaper 1.0.0: convective and severe-weather parameters from gridded data (ERA5) for Python 3.10+
description:
xcaper is a modernised and extended derivative of xcape (Lepore, Allen & Abernathey; v0.1.4, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5270332). It computes convective and severe-weather parameters on gridded datasets, mainly ERA5 reanalysis, from numpy, dask or xarray arrays. Fortran kernels run alongside a numba backend, and large domains are processed in parallel chunks with dask.

What is new compared with xcape 0.1.4

  • Builds on modern Python (meson-python instead of numpy.distutils), with support for NumPy 2. The Fortran compiler is optional: without one, a pure numba backend gives the same results to round-off.
  • Bug fixes in the original code: uninitialised accumulators in the Bunkers storm-motion routine, a broken dask pathway for pressure-level data, and unsafe STOP/PRINT statements in the Fortran kernels.
  • New parameters: surface-based, mixed-layer and most-unstable CAPE and CIN; LCL, LFC and equilibrium level; DCAPE; lapse rates (virtual temperature); Bunkers storm motion (standard 0–6 km, shallow 0–3 km, or effective-layer after Bunkers et al. 2014); storm-relative helicity, bulk wind difference, critical angle; streamwise vorticity and streamwiseness.
  • Effective inflow layer (Thompson et al. 2007) and its parameters: ESRH, EBWD, effective-layer streamwise vorticity and streamwiseness, ESCP and ESTP. Fixed-layer SCP, STP, EHI and WMAXSHEAR are also included.
  • An ERA5 workflow: download a bounding box from the Copernicus Climate Data Store, combine the single-level and pressure-level fields, compute 64 parameters, and write CF-compliant NetCDF. It is available as a Python API and as a command-line tool (xcaper-era5).

Validation

  • 116 automated tests, plus the unchanged xcape 0.1.4 test suite (all passing).
  • The Fortran results reproduce xcape 0.1.4 exactly for CAPE, CIN, heights and Bunkers motion (SRH to 1e-13). The numba backend matches the Fortran backend to round-off (CAPE within 0.25 J/kg; CIN can differ only where parcel buoyancy touches zero within single-precision resolution, 2 of 29,141 test columns).
  • On an ERA5 case over the Philippine region (29,141 columns): the effective inflow layer is identical to a brute-force search; DCAPE agrees with MetPy to within 0.3% (median); LFC and EL agree to within 1 hPa (median); lapse rates match SounderPy.
  • Identical results on Python 3.10–3.14 and with the oldest and newest supported dependency versions (Linux x86_64); the Python 3.15 pre-release also passes.

Conventions and limitations

  • CIN is reported as a positive number. Composite indices use right-mover SRH (Northern Hemisphere convention).
  • The mixed-layer parcel is 500 m deep and the most-unstable parcel is taken below 500 hPa; both differ from the SPC conventions (100 hPa and 300 hPa).
  • ESCP and ESTP follow the SPC/SHARPpy definitions. Effective composites from other tools that use different shear layers will not match.

Credits. Parcel ascent: George H. Bryan's getcape (NCAR/UCAR). Original xcape by Chiara Lepore, John Allen and Ryan Abernathey. Parameter definitions follow Bunkers et al. (2000, 2014), Thompson et al. (2003, 2004, 2007, 2012) and Taszarek et al. (2020).
